8:["$","$L13",null,{"data":{"chapterId":21,"verseId":20,"chapterTitle":"Examination of Becoming and Destruction","totalVerses":21,"verseData":{"id":"v21_20","number":20,"title":"If Becoming and Destruction Had Inherent Existence, Bondage and Liberation Would Be Impossible","sanskrit":{"text":"","transliteration":"","translation":"If becoming and destruction had inherent existence, then bondage and liberation would be impossible. Bondage and liberation require the possibility of change."},"philosophy":{"insight":"The SOTERIOLOGICAL consequence: if becoming/destruction were inherent, BONDAGE (samsara) and LIBERATION (nirvana) would be impossible. Both require change — bondage is the process of being caught; liberation is the process of being freed. Emptiness of becoming/destruction is necessary for the Buddhist path.","madhyamaka":"Saṃbhava vibhava svabhāva cet, bandha mokṣa na sambhava (if becoming/destruction had inherent existence, bondage and liberation wouldn't be possible). Both bandha and mokṣa are processes that involve change. Inherent processes can't change → no bondage or liberation.","quantum":"Quantum state preparation and measurement: preparing a quantum state (like preparing for liberation) requires the ability to change the system. If quantum states were inherently fixed, no preparation or measurement would be possible — the system would be frozen.","bridge":"Both quantum state manipulation and v.20 show that change is necessary for \"preparation\" (liberation). QM: inherently fixed states can't be prepared/measured. V.20: inherent becoming/destruction blocks bondage/liberation. Both: transformation requires the absence of inherent fixity.","accessible":"If \"being locked in a room\" were inherent, you could never escape. If \"escaping\" were inherent, you'd never be locked in the first place. Both bondage and liberation require the POSSIBILITY of change — which requires emptiness.","twoTruths":"Conventionally: beings are in bondage and can achieve liberation through practice. Ultimately: both bondage and liberation are empty of inherent existence — which is precisely what makes the transition possible.","commonMisconception":"NOT saying bondage and liberation are illusory. They're conventionally real. V.20 says their possibility DEPENDS on the emptiness of becoming/destruction.
